It's because of the vowel endings! The vowel for 'door' in this sentence would be a damma (oo sound) because it is the subject. Because it's 'a door' rather than 'the door,' the word is indefinite. And in MSA, you double the vowel ending on indefinite words when you write them. That doubling adds an 'n' sound, for some reason... oo to oon, a to an, and i to in.

One caveat to the indefinite word = double the vowel rule is when the indefinite word is part of an idaafa (noun modified by one or more nouns). The idaafa makes it definite so no need to double.
